In high school we played basketball in winter in our down jackets. After a snowfall the court was unplayable, so we’d haul out brooms and shovels and clear everything inside the three-point line. Some of us wore hats and gloves. Go without gloves, and the snow stuck to the ball would melt in your hands; stop touching the ball for a minute and it froze into a thin crust of ice.

Back in the classroom, drenched in sweat and still wrapped in our down jackets, we’d slowly dry out. Steam would start rising from the tops of our heads, as if we had seized the throne and ascended to immortality.

You’re asking if we feel the cold?

Damn right we do. We’re freezing our butts off!
